decisions.issues: v12 is the pick. Nagoji is on the left and matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, loose curly hair, ochre rags, bandaged wrists. Keshavrao is on the right with short hair, a grey-brown tunic and no ear stud, but his moustache is a little heavier than the 'faint' one on his sheet. Both haul a taut pen chain level in their manacled fists with their heels braced on the pen plank. The chain rises to the ring, which hangs by its last bolt from a splintered beam at upper right. That matches the ring's position and damage in 5.1, 5.2 and 4.5, and the pull is on their fists and shoulders, with no upward pull on any neck. There is no painted text, no noose and no gore, and the hands are sound. The dark ceiling from the upper middle to the upper left (about x 0.33 to 0.80, y 0.02 to 0.25) gives clear room for both Nagoji balloons. Minor flaws: (1) The water only splashes around the plank at ankle height, shallower than the waist-deep flood in 4.5 and 5.3. The ship's roll can explain it, but it is a small continuity drift. (2) Each ankle cuff has its own dangling chain stub instead of one short hobble chain joining the ankles. (3) The pull runs across the frame rather than toward the camera. (4) The pen chain runs to the collars by short drop-chains rather than threading through the collars' side rings, which slightly weakens the run-back in 5.5. v04 is rejected. Its ring is intact on an undamaged bracket, so the 'last bolt' beat is lost. The ring's chain also hangs straight down and slack, which contradicts the haul, and no pen plank is shown.
